plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with conservative limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to zero.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Focus on capital preservation and lower drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Reduce all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to smaller allocations.
This reduces overall leverage and concentration towards a balanced approach.
Buy TZA at 4% as a new long setup from the scanner.
Maintain a blend of broad index, quality tech, and small leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new scanner-identified long setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, balancing growth with risk management.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Increase exposure to existing leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to 6% each.
Buy TZA at 6% as a new high-risk/reward long setup from the scanner.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
Strict stop discipline is critical due to amplified risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by increasing leverage and concentration. It raises both upside potential and drawdown risk significantly. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for higher income potential.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to zero.
This rotates the portfolio towards income-generating assets and away from high-beta names.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan aims to park cash for yield, targeting ~1% per month. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown by focusing on income ETFs and cutting high-beta, leveraged positions. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
